## Iterative ontology construction via conversation

With [ontologyAPI](https://github.com/CathalByrneGit/ontologyAPI) installed,
you can add the discovery session to an MCP server as a tool and build the
ontology through a conversation with any MCP-capable assistant.

```{r setup}
library(ontologyDiscoverR)
# remotes::install_github("CathalByrneGit/ontologyAPI")  # optional companion package
```

## Setting up the MCP server

`ontologyAPI::mcp_server()` serves an existing bundle and its data. Add the
discovery tool to it with `dis_add_mcp_tool()`, which registers
`build_ontology` through `ontologyAPI::mcp_add_tool()`. The tool uses the
session's LLM provider unless you pass another one with `llm =`.

```{r mcp}
sess <- discover_session("mcp-demo", llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1"))

svc    <- ontologyAPI::ontology_service(existing_bundle, con)
server <- ontologyAPI::mcp_server(svc, name = "ontology-builder")
dis_add_mcp_tool(server, sess)                 # adds "build_ontology"
pop_add_mcp_tool(server, pop_sess)             # optional: adds "query_population"
ontologyAPI::serve_mcp(server, transport = "stdio")
```

The server is modified in place, so the return value of `dis_add_mcp_tool()`
can be ignored.

## Example conversation flow

Once the server is running, an LLM agent can interact with it:

```
User: "Look at this database schema and build me an ontology for a hospital"
Assistant: [parses schema, calls dis_extract, lists discovered types]

User: "The Patient table also connects to the Ward table via ward_assignments"
Assistant: [calls build_ontology("Add a link from Patient to Ward called ward_assignments, many_to_many")]
→ Done: Added link type 'ward_assignments'

User: "Add a concept for high-risk patients: age > 65 OR previous_admissions > 0"
Assistant: [calls build_ontology("Add concept high_risk_patient for Patient where age > 65 OR previous_admissions > 0")]
→ Done: Added concept hint 'high_risk_patient'

User: "Looks good — approve everything and generate the bundle"
Assistant: [calls build_ontology("Approve all pending object types"), then dis_to_bundle()]
```

## Supported natural language instructions

The `build_ontology` tool understands:

| Instruction pattern | Effect |
|---|---|
| `"Add an object type for X with properties a, b, c"` | Adds a CandidateObjectType |
| `"Add a link from X to Y called Z"` | Adds a CandidateLinkType |
| `"Add a concept called X for Y where <SQL condition>"` | Adds a CandidateConceptHint |
| `"Add an action called X on Y"` | Adds a CandidateActionType |
| `"Approve all pending object types"` | Sets status = approved |
| `"Reject the concept high_risk"` | Sets status = rejected for that id |

## Getting the bundle

Ask for it in the conversation ("Generate the bundle as hospital-v1"). The tool
calls `dis_to_bundle()`, which builds the bundle with the ontologySpecR
constructors and validates it, and reports any validation problem back to the
assistant, naming the candidate that caused it.
